fixtures.label: Multi-destination
fixtures.description: The only MULTI-DESTINATION fixture, and it is hand-built because it has to be: measured 2026-08-14 over the 200 most recent dev orders, every single one has exactly one destination, so this shape cannot be captured. Do not "clean it up" into a capture. Two destinations — customer-collecting from our counter (charge window == delivery window) plus a we-deliver stage with a divergent charge window — which is the only thing that exercises per-destination banner rows in the items table, the legend variants, and the conditional Dates Charged row. Items, prices and taxes are drawn from real orders; the organization, contacts and instructions are invented and both addresses are public corporate venues, so it is PII-free by construction and is NOT run through applyPii.

fixtures.label: Discounts + transaction fee
fixtures.description: The money-coverage fixture: a percent discount, a flat (dollars-per-unit) discount, and a percent_of_total transaction fee — the three shapes no other fixture exercises, which left 5 of quote.eta's 19 it.currency sites in branches nothing renders. Every money value is computed by @cfs/core/utils/orders rather than typed by hand. Organization, contacts and instructions are invented and the address is a public venue, so it is PII-free by construction.

fixtures.label: Service only, untaxed
fixtures.description: The 6-column floor: the only fixture that drops BOTH the Duration and the Tax column. One untaxed service line, no rental anywhere, no discount — so every conditional column in the items grid is off and the header is just Item Description / Type / Qty / Unit Price / Subtotal / Total. Note it is NOT "the only fixture without tax" — rental-discount-exempt drops Tax too but keeps Duration. Captured from prod order 977.

fixtures.label: Taxed sale, no rentals
fixtures.description: 7 columns — Tax on, Duration and Discount off. A single taxed sale line and no rental anywhere, so this is the only fixture that renders a Tax column with NO Duration column beside it, and the only one whose grid is exactly one conditional wide. Captured from prod order 992.

fixtures.label: Discounted rentals, tax exempt
fixtures.description: 8 columns via Duration + Discount with Tax OFF — the only fixture that lays a Discount column out with no Tax column next to it, because the organization is tax_exempt and totals.taxes is empty. Two of its five rentals are 100% discounted, so subtotal_discounted_cents is 0: the falsy-zero case that made `||` print the pre-discount subtotal. Also carries two sibling groups under one destination. templates#69 listed this order as 9 columns; measured 2026-08-14 it is 8. Captured from prod order 989.

fixtures.label: Taxed rental, no discount
fixtures.description: 8 columns via Duration + Tax with Discount OFF — the commonest real shape (a taxed rental order nobody discounted) and the only fixture in the family that renders it. templates#69 dropped this order believing mixed-two-tax-rates covered the same combination; measured 2026-08-14 that order carries a 100%-discounted line and renders 9 columns, so without this entry the set had no Duration+Tax 8-column case at all and the two 8-column shapes collapsed to one. Deliberately minimal — one rental in one group — because its job is the column combination, not content. Captured from prod order 991.

fixtures.label: Two tax rates, mixed item types
fixtures.description: The only fixture with TWO tax rates in one order — Chicago Rental Tax 15% on the rentals and Chicago Sales Tax 10.25% on the sales — so it is the only one where the totals block emits more than a single tax row. Also the widest item-type spread in the family: rental, sale, replacement, service and surcharge in one document, with the service and surcharge untaxed beside taxed lines, plus repeated product uids across rows. It renders 9 columns (a 100%-discounted rental turns the Discount column on); rental-discount-taxed and long-multi-group share that count and are kept for different reasons — see their descriptions. Captured from prod order 993.

fixtures.label: 9-column ceiling, single page
fixtures.description: The 9-column ceiling readable in a single view: Duration, Discount and Tax all on, over four rentals in one group with one 20% discount and 15% rental tax. This is the fixture for eyeballing column widths under `table-layout: fixed` — the tightest grid the template can produce, small enough to take in at once. long-multi-group renders the same nine columns but over ~90 rows across several pages, which answers a different question (page breaks, not widths); a reader who sees only the column count will otherwise delete one of the two as a duplicate. Captured from prod order 943.

fixtures.label: Long order: page breaks + components
fixtures.description: The only fixture under PAGE-BREAK pressure and the only one with real components — two things no other fixture in the family has. ~90 items across 10 groups on one destination, 24 charge days, plus a second long table below it (replacement total $28,847.87), so it is the only fixture that shows group banner rows recurring across pages and whether the items header repeats. It is also the component-indentation fixture: 31 line items are nested under another LINE ITEM rather than under a divider (the Rolling Set Kit carries 16, the pop-up tent 6), which is what the one-em-per-level indent exists to render — every other fixture bottoms out at a group, so the indent is uniformly 0 and the code is unexercised. Brings a third tax profile (tax_rantoul, Rantoul Sales Tax) and `custom-` prefixed line uids alongside repeated product uids. It is the largest file in the repo by a wide margin; that is the cost of the only page-break and component coverage there is, so do not hand-trim it or it stops being a captured document. Captured from prod order 985.
